li.label: played Ur clueless
li.description: I pushed the little pieces around the board for a while. I honestly have no idea how this game works. It was nice to sit down, at least.

li.label: starting to get Ur
li.description: I think I finally understand what the rosettes do. You land on one, you go again. That's most of it, right?

li.label: played a decent game of Ur
li.description: I held the middle square for three turns and nobody could touch me. There's more to this old game than it looks.

li.label: played Ur well
li.description: I can see two moves ahead now. You don't run a piece into the shared row unless you've counted what the other side can roll.

li.label: rarely loses at Ur
li.description: People have stopped asking me to play. I keep telling them it's mostly the dice. It is not mostly the dice.

li.label: mastered the game of Ur
li.description: Four thousand five hundred years of this game, and I have it solved. Seven pieces, fourteen squares, and not one wasted roll.

li.label: threw horseshoes badly
li.description: Most of them landed nowhere near the pin. One went into the dirt about a metre short. Good arm exercise.

li.label: getting the hang of horseshoes
li.description: You have to let it turn once in the air. Once I stopped throwing it flat, they started landing close.

li.label: threw a decent round
li.description: Two leaners and a ringer. Not bad for standing in a field flinging metal at a stick.

li.label: threw horseshoes well
li.description: I know the distance in my shoulder now. I do not have to think about it any more.

li.label: rarely misses the pin
li.description: Somebody bet me a meal I could not ring three in a row. I am eating well tonight.

li.label: mastered horseshoes
li.description: Twelve metres, a lump of iron, and a stick in the ground. There is nothing left in it I do not know.

li.label: threw stones at a ring
li.description: I threw stones at a ring for a while and none of them went through. Somebody said that is normal at first.

li.label: getting the hang of hoopstone
li.description: The trick is the arc, not the speed. Throw it flat and it just clangs off the rim.

li.label: put a few through
li.description: Three clean through the ring today. You hear it when it goes through without touching.

li.label: threw hoopstone well
li.description: I can pick my stone by weight now and know where it will land before it leaves my hand.

li.label: rarely misses the ring
li.description: People come to watch rather than play. It is a little embarrassing. I keep throwing.

li.label: mastered hoopstone
li.description: A stone, a ring, and the space between them. I have not missed in a long time.

li.label: knocked the balls around
li.description: I hit the white one and the others went somewhere. I am told that is not the whole game.

li.label: learning the table
li.description: You do not aim at the ball, you aim at where the ball has to be hit. That took me an embarrassingly long time.

li.label: sank a few
li.description: Three in a row off the same rail. Somebody actually stopped to watch.

li.label: plays a good game
li.description: I am starting to think about where the cue ball ends up, not just whether the shot drops.

li.label: rarely misses
li.description: Nobody wants to break against me any more. I keep offering.

li.label: mastered the table
li.description: Nine balls and six pockets. I can see the whole run before I take the first shot.

li.label: pushed chess pieces around
li.description: I moved the little horse in an L shape because someone told me that is what it does. I lost. I am not sure when I lost, only that it had already happened.

li.label: learning chess
li.description: I stopped leaving pieces where they could be taken for free. That alone made the whole game feel different.

li.label: played a solid game of chess
li.description: I traded down into an endgame and pushed a pawn all the way. Watching it come back as a queen never gets old.

li.label: played chess well
li.description: I saw the fork two moves before it was there, and I let them walk into it. Sixty-four squares and I owned about forty of them.

li.label: rarely loses at chess
li.description: They keep opening with the same thing. I keep answering with the same thing. They keep resigning around move thirty.

li.label: mastered chess
li.description: I have started announcing the mate before I play the move that forces it. Nobody sits down with me twice.
